entries.8e76bb8434d505bf: Toward 2030, the company has set the society to which DIC contributes as "Green," "Digital" and "Quality of Life (QOL)," and its policy is to concentrate management resources on business areas where it can leverage its strengths. The basic strategies of its long-term management plan "DIC Vision 2030" are the transformation of its business portfolio and its sustainability strategy. In the transformation of its business portfolio, the company says it will raise the earning power of its core businesses through structural reform and product portfolio conversion of inks and packaging materials, pigments and polymers, and will position chemtronics and composites/devices as growth businesses supporting an "AI-integrated society" in which AI merges into the mechanisms of society, providing materials and solutions mainly in the fields of semiconductors, batteries and physical AI. Its sustainability strategy consists of the development of sustainable products, the reduction of CO2 emissions, and responses to the circular economy. Fiscal 2026 to fiscal 2030 is the final phase (Phase2), in which the company says it will invest resources intensively in growth businesses while raising the earning power of its core businesses.

entries.a84d3eb83e7cf12b: A business that manufactures and sells pigments for paints, plastics, inks, specialty uses, color filters and cosmetics, as well as health food products. Revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥215,192 million (¥218,075 million in the previous year). Pigments for paints and pigments for plastics, which account for a large share of revenue, saw shipments fall as demand stalled, centered on Europe and the United States, amid uncertainty over the economic outlook; however, revenue rose through efforts to revise prices. Pigments for color filters saw shipments fall below the prior year as panel manufacturers' operating rates remained unstable, but revenue rose due to the effect of product mix. Pigments for cosmetics saw revenue decline due to stagnant demand from cosmetics manufacturers in Europe and the United States. Pigments for specialty uses saw revenue rise as shipments for agricultural applications recovered and construction applications also grew. Outside pigments, revenue from liquid crystal material products declined because the company withdrew from the liquid crystal materials business.

entries.fa61d56d687b8733: A business that manufactures and sells printing inks, such as gravure inks, offset inks, newspaper inks and jet inks, and packaging materials, such as polystyrene, adhesives for packaging materials and multilayer films; it is the reporting segment with the largest revenue from external customers. Revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥549,677 million (¥560,108 million in the previous year, a 1.9% decrease year on year). Packaging inks used for food packaging saw shipments fall in Japan and in the Americas and Europe, but revenue rose in both regions as pricing measures continued. Publication inks used for commercial printing and newspapers saw revenue decline as demand for publications continued to fall in each region, while jet inks used for digital printing saw revenue rise as digitalization progressed. From the fiscal year ended December 2025, part of the management classification was revised, and some consolidated subsidiaries moved from this segment to 'Functional Products'. Prior-year figures are restated to the revised classification for comparison.
entries.fc57a3f122439e5f: Seiko PMC traces back to a company established in 1968 as a joint venture for the paper chemicals business. In January 2024, all shares held by the company were transferred through an acquisition of treasury shares by that company (later renamed CHEMIPAZ Corporation).
entries.fed18c87d9612d47: The new Sun Chemical is currently a consolidated subsidiary.
